items.title: Buddy Burns and Frank Pasley Interview, 1968-09-23
items.q: Oh, yeah. I think her name is Helen.

ctx.x: Do you know when? About 18 years ago. 18 years ago? Mm-hmm. About 18 and 19 years ago. You met him still here in California? No, I know him in New Orleans when I was in short pants. He was older than you? About one year. Oh, only one year. Yeah. Oh, my God, I know him a long time. Somebody told me his real name was Joseph Caillou. Could that be?

Could be, but all I know, we call him, everybody called him Red Caillou. Yeah. That's, you know. He was a light fella? Yeah. Yeah. Real light fella. Did he have a- Short. Little short. Yeah. Freckles on his face. Do you know when he moved to California? About 1925 or 26. Oh, yeah. Very interesting. I bought his wife's family. Yeah, he's got a wife. She played too up there in Oakland. Oh, she's still up there? Yeah, she's still up there. Oh. Yeah. In Oakland. Oakland County. What's her name? I forgot. But she's up…

Two months ago. I saw him three weeks ago. He's living on South Ingalls side of him. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. Oliver. He's a good friend of little brother Montgomery. Yeah. Just be honest with that. Yeah. His brother's in New Orleans. Yeah. Alvin, I know. Alvin, yeah. What can you tell me about Oliver Alcorn? Well, we raised up together. His father bought him a C melody saxophone. Yeah.
